chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Geneva band job and a missed share in a highway deal
summary: After the venture failed he took a band to Geneva for two months, met a man proposing a huge Ivory Coast to Dakar highway, did not ask for a share, then decided to come home.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, we stayed there and we made it pretty good and everything was right. Well, I said, now, I done lost this money. There's no point in me staying here. I've got to move on. So I went back to Paris and he said, well, Jacques, we'll try to salvage this. Just leave. So I said okay, and I went back to Paris, stayed in Paris. And something said, Jacques, you go home, go home. I got a job with the Belgian -- not the Belgian, I mean I had a friend who played saxophone in Geneva, Switzerland. And the business buddy of mine there). I went there, Geneva, Switzerland, I took this band and went to Geneva, stayed two months. And that is where I met this man who said he wanted to build a highway from -- (Ivory Coast) I think it was from Abidjan (ETIC) to the big city of (Dakar) Senegal. And that was about a six or eight billion dollar thing, and I was so dumb in this business, I didn't ask for five percent. (Inaudible).
So then I finished there and I stayed around Paris,
you know, about a year. And then I decided to come home (inaudible). When I come back to America I said, my goodness.
